editorial.headline: Employer Pension Funds: A Clear PMA Position in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This conventional employer pension-fund activity is nationally open to PMA and is not blocked by Bali’s risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 65301 covers the conventional management of an employer pension fund. It is an activity established by a person or entity that employs staff, acting as the founder, to run a pension programme for some or all of its employees. The programme may be a defined-benefit pension programme or a defined-contribution pension programme. The essential structure is employer-founded and employee-facing: the fund exists for participating employees and creates an obligation for the employer.

The people or entities registering under it are therefore employers setting up and managing the conventional fund they have formed. The record opens the activity at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Those labels span the full scale range stated for the activity, while its purpose remains precise: serving some or all of the founder’s employees through either a defined-benefit or defined-contribution arrangement. Whether participation covers part of the workforce or all employees is built into the stated scope.

At the national level, this activity has TERBUKA PMA status and a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record allows full foreign ownership for this activity. Bali does not reverse that conclusion. Its entry is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record notes that, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Medium-High/High; the activity is therefore not blocked by Bali’s island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. Nationally, the activity is open to PMA with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, and in Bali it is not blocked by the island-wide moratorium.

The distinction between the national allowance and Bali treatment should remain intact. The 100% ceiling is the national PMA figure. Bali’s entry gives a risk-based reason for the absence of a moratorium block at Besar scale, rather than a separate ownership percentage or partnership condition. The appropriate reading is direct: conventional employer pension-fund management is nationally open to PMA, and Bali’s permanent Low and Medium-Low risk PMA moratorium does not block this activity.
